sources.note: Nothing on Dai stress. p.224: 'The languages of the Babar node are poorly documented. The 193-item word lists in Taber (1993) are the only source of data for five of these languages: Dai [dij], North Babar [bcd], East Marsela [vme], Imroing [imr], and Tela-Masbuar [tvm].' p.226 + fn.32 quote Dai phonetic forms with Taber's stress marks ([ˈaʈʰon] 'dog', [n̩ˈnoʈ] 'run', [ˈnoʈnon] 'rattan', [ˈnɛvriʈ] 'bathe', [n̩ˈpuʈ] 'rotten', [ˈdutʔon] 'breast', [ˈmatʰʔɛˈnon] 'smoke') only for a [d]~[ʈ] allophony argument. Generic remark elsewhere (Flores chapter) that penultimate stress is the normal rule for…

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023a. Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands. Endangered Languages Archive deposit emplawas-edwards-0741, hdl:2196/28f40694-81ac-4d06-b515-617dd6469394.
sources.note: Deposit landing page lists 13 languages (Emplawas, Imroing, Tela-Masbuar, SE Babar, North Babar, Serili, East/West/Central Marsela, Teun, Nila, Serua, Seluwasan, Makatian); Dai is not among them, consistent with Grimes & Edwards 2026 fn.26. Nothing on Dai.

sources.citation: Taber, Mark. 1993. Toward a better understanding of the indigenous languages of Southwestern Maluku. Oceanic Linguistics 32(2): 389-441 — the 193-item Dai wordlist (Hartuti/Hertuti village) as re-keyed with Taber's stress marks in Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer (eds.) 2019, LexiRumah 3.0.0 (CLDF), lect daii1240.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Primary data only, no prose. Every polysyllable carries a stress mark: 106 penult (ˈne-on 'sun', ˈwunn-on 'moon', ˈtakn-on 'knife', naˈnorɛn 'sea'), 63 with the mark on the last syllable (suˈʔ-on 'wind', raˈʔ-on 'blood', anˈon 'child', ɛsˈon 'person', horˈhor 'near', peˈpen 'full'; ~20 of these are verbs/adjectives like n̩ˈmat 'die', n̩ˈpuʈ 'rotten' whose only other nucleus is a syllabic nasal prefix), 1 antepenult, 5 double-marked, 18 monosyllables (tabulation). The article text itself (transcription conventions) was not accessible (JSTOR).
